title: 《发哨子的人》：刊载、失去可见性、文本变体与记忆幸存的初步来源登记
methodological_warning: Published page metadata, cached reprints, journalist descriptions of unavailability, and original-platform evidence are distinct. No original WeChat article URL or verified bytes of its 2020-03-10 first edition are established. nCovMemory CSV row 3142 records a candidate original WeChat URL and archive link but their original content remains unverified.

privacy: No copied unredacted chat logs, patients' reports, private family identifiers or full copyrighted interview text. Public URLs only; no private screenshots.
originality_boundary: Sun & Wright (2023 online, 2024 issue) already study relay activism on WeChat/GitHub. The current pilot asks which platform/edition and secondary-journalism claims are independently authenticatable, particularly the eight-person police-label conflation across cases. Wu (2024) also identifies textual, multimodal and technically encoded relay tactics. Avoid repackaging these findings; prioritize source-version attestation and labeled-actor conflation with cross-case corrections. Source discovery: known WeChat URL improves targeted authentication but does not establish exact original text.
